title: Basic tokens in unpadded or URL-safe Base64 forms
summary: Three synthetic tokens after the Basic scheme: one with its padding removed, one in the URL-safe alphabet and one whose value has been split by a space.
rationale: token68 admits the URL-safe alphabet and unpadded values while Basic's Base64 is the standard alphabet with padding; a recipient may accept, repair or reject these forms. Whether such a string is a Basic credential, and where a split value ends, is not stated, so no extent is frozen.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted. RFC 9110 token68 admits unpadded and URL-safe forms, RFC 7617 specifies standard Base64, and the sources do not say how a recipient handles the difference or a value split by whitespace.

sources.supports: token68 can hold a base64, base64url, base32, or base16 encoding, with or without padding, but excluding whitespace
Base 64 Encoding with URL and Filename Safe Alphabet is a distinct encoding from the standard Base 64 Encoding

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited standards read on 2026-10-03, before any scanner was consulted. All values are synthetic and were not tested against any service. Header coalescing, parser and action policy, decoded-token mapping and product masking stay with the downstream repositories.
